Align raw taxon names to a prepared taxonomic reference

Source: R/align_taxa.R
align_taxa.Rd

Attempts to match each name in original_name to a name in resources (produced by prepare_taxonomic_resources()), trying, in order, exact matches (scientific name with authorship, then canonical name), then progressively more lenient fuzzy matches, at species level first and then at each higher taxonomic rank present in resources. See match_taxa() for the full sequence of match attempts.

Usage

align_taxa(
  original_name,
  resources = NULL,
  identifier = NA_character_,
  fuzzy_abs_dist = 3,
  fuzzy_rel_dist = 0.2,
  fuzzy_matches = TRUE,
  imprecise_fuzzy_matches = FALSE,
  taxon_ranks_to_check = NULL,
  hybrids = TRUE,
  intergrades_affinis = TRUE,
  consider_english_name_endings = FALSE,
  include_bracketed_info = TRUE,
  progress = FALSE,
  full = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

original_name

Character vector of raw taxon names to align.

resources

The taxonomic reference to align against: the nested list produced by prepare_taxonomic_resources(), or a reference table (or a list of them, such as load_taxonomic_resources()'s output), which is run through prepare_taxonomic_resources() automatically. Preparing it yourself first saves repeating that work when aligning several name lists against the same reference.

identifier

A dataset, location or other identifier associated with each name in original_name – used only to disambiguate genus sp.-style aligned names (see prepare_taxonomic_resources()/match_taxa()) as belonging to a specific dataset/location. Recycled if length 1; otherwise must be the same length as original_name. Defaults to NA.

fuzzy_abs_dist

The number of characters allowed to differ for a fuzzy match.

fuzzy_rel_dist

The proportion of characters allowed to differ for a fuzzy match.

fuzzy_matches

Logical; whether fuzzy matching is attempted at all. Defaults to TRUE.

imprecise_fuzzy_matches

Logical; reserved for a more lenient fuzzy-matching pass (not yet implemented – see match_taxa()). Defaults to FALSE.

taxon_ranks_to_check

Optional character vector of taxonomic ranks (besides species) to attempt higher-rank matches against. Defaults to NULL, which uses every higher rank present in resources.

hybrids

Logical; if TRUE (the default, as APCalign always does), a hybrid name (Genus x species) that isn't itself a listed name is resolved to genus rank ("Genus x [original name]") rather than left for later match attempts – with FALSE, "Banksia serrata x ericifolia" aligns to Banksia serrata. See ?match_taxa.

intergrades_affinis

Logical; if TRUE (the default, as APCalign always does), names suggesting an intergrade (--), an indecision between taxa (/), or a graded/"affinis"/"cf." identification are resolved to genus rank the same way, unless the whole name is a listed name. See ?match_taxa.

consider_english_name_endings

Logical; if TRUE, before any fuzzy matching, try substituting a recognised informal English vernacular name ending (e.g. "-id", "-ine", "-oid") for its formal Latin equivalent and attempt an exact match on the corrected name. Defaults to FALSE. See ?match_taxa.

include_bracketed_info

Logical; TRUE (the default) gives every higher-rank-only match APCalign's "<rank name> sp. [<original name>; <identifier>]" form, e.g. "Banksia sp. [Banksia]" for a bare "Banksia". FALSE drops the brackets when the name is nothing more than the matched rank's own name (a bare single word, or a bare "Genus (Subgenus)"), giving just "Banksia"; original_name keeps the raw input either way, and a name with anything more keeps the brackets regardless. See ?match_taxa.

progress

Logical; if TRUE, prints a text progress bar tracking what fraction of original_name has been resolved so far. Useful for large inputs, where matching can take a while. Defaults to FALSE. See ?match_taxa.

full

Logical; if TRUE, return every intermediate column match_taxa() computes (useful for inspecting why a name matched the way it did). If FALSE (the default), return just the key output columns.

quiet

Accepted for compatibility with APCalign's function of the same name; this function prints nothing either way.

Value

A tibble with one row per element of original_name (preserving its length, order and any duplicates/NAs), with columns original_name, cleaned_name, aligned_name, taxonomic_dataset, taxon_rank, taxonomic_status, taxon_ID, accepted_name_usage_ID, aligned_reason, alignment_code, chars_changed and identifier (or, if full = TRUE, every column match_taxa() computes along the way). taxon_ID/accepted_name_usage_ID identify which row of resources a name matched to, and are what update_taxa() uses to resolve a matched synonym forward to its current accepted name. chars_changed is the number of characters that differed between the name being matched and the reference name it matched – 0 for every exact match, the actual edit distance (Damerau-Levenshtein) for a fuzzy match, and NA when nothing matched at all.

Examples

reference <- data.frame(
  canonical_name = c("Boronia", "Boronia serrulata", "Boronia oldname"),
  scientific_name = c("Boronia Sm.", "Boronia serrulata Sm.", "Boronia oldname Sm."),
  taxon_rank = c("genus", "species", "species"),
  taxonomic_status = c("accepted", "accepted", "synonym"),
  taxonomic_dataset = "MY_LIST", genus = "Boronia",
  taxon_ID = c("1", "2", "3"), accepted_name_usage_ID = c("1", "2", "2")
)
# a misspelling and a synonym
aligned <- align_taxa(c("Boronia serulata", "Boronia oldname"), reference)
aligned[, c("original_name", "aligned_name", "taxonomic_status", "aligned_reason")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   original_name    aligned_name      taxonomic_status aligned_reason            
#>   <chr>            <chr>             <chr>            <chr>                     
#> 1 Boronia serulata Boronia serrulata accepted         Fuzzy match of taxon name…
#> 2 Boronia oldname  Boronia oldname   synonym          Exact match of taxon name…
